moduleTitle: Theory Lesson - Introduction to Test Data Service
learningObjectives: Distinguish a repository, a TDS type and an individual item.
Explain explicit TDS operations and the difference between application state and stored test-data state.
Plan selection and locking for a stateful test workflow.
Trace an independent order example without assuming automatic synchronization.

elements.description: TDS manages test data in distributed environments. Its web interface shows the types in a selected repository and the items in a selected type; access may be restricted by authorization.

elements.title: Repository → type → item
items: Repository: the configured data store selected by the test.
Type: a category containing test items, such as CustomerDetails.
Item: one data entry within that category.
Status: in our practice example, an ordinary application-defined property, not proof of execution success or a built-in synchronization mechanism.

bulletPoints: A type groups items; it is not an individual item or the entire repository.

studyGuide.sectionTitle: How Tosca Commander and TDS talk to each other

elements.description: Standard Modules create, find, update, move and delete test items. The test configuration selects the service and repository. API Scan can also manage test data using the installed service definition.

An application action does not automatically synchronize a TDS property. Model the application action, verify its result, and explicitly write the needed test-data state. The web data view is not a test execution report.

Suppose one test creates a practice user, another prepares a file, and a third uploads it. Record the actual identifiers needed by later steps. For a focused upload test, provide a suitable user and file during setup rather than assuming the whole journey must always run first.
Find & provide item selects a matching item and locks it for the test. ReadOnly in the Expert Module reads without acquiring that lock; it is not an unlock operation.

elements.text: Find releases its lock after execution, on failure or at a new loop iteration. A lock coordinates TDS item access; it is not proof of an application-level database transaction or permanent consumption.

elements.title: A synthetic workflow to reason about
items: Prepare a disposable customer and address.
Create a basket and place an order through the application.
Capture the actual order identifier and verify the application result.
Write the required TDS properties explicitly.
After completing the scenario, deliberately move the known item to a Used type if that is your reuse policy.

elements.text: This is a Quilyn teaching example, not a verified Academy video transcript or executed DemoWebShop walkthrough. Status, OrderStatus and Used are example names rather than automatic TDS lifecycle rules.

elements.description: Suppose the purchase test has successfully obtained an order identifier and its next TDS Update step is configured to add OrderNumber and set OrderStatus to Pending. That step writes those properties. The application purchase alone does not do it, and completion does not automatically move the item.

bulletPoints: Verify application actions separately from TDS updates.
Use appropriate preconditions, selection criteria and a deliberate reuse policy.

examPitfalls.title: Confusing a type with an item
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Treating a category such as CustomerDetails as one test-data entry.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: A repository contains types; a type contains items.

examPitfalls.title: Assuming automatic state synchronization
examPitfalls.trapDescription: Expecting an application purchase or successful test to update Status or move the item without a TDS operation.
examPitfalls.bestPractice: Verify the application result and explicitly update or move the known item. Prepare dependencies in setup for focused tests.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In TDS terminology, what does a 'TDS type' represent?

options.text: An individual row of test data.
A category of test records within a repository, e.g. CustomerDetails or SampleOfOrders.
The name of the entire database.
The current state of one record, such as New or Active.

practiceQuiz.hint: Distinguish the container category from one entry.
practiceQuiz.rationale: A TDS type groups items within a selected repository. An individual item and an example Status property are different concepts.

optionExplanations.A: One row or data entry is an item, not the category that contains it.
optionExplanations.B: A type is the category of items inside the selected repository.
optionExplanations.C: The repository is the containing configured data store, not one of its types.
optionExplanations.D: New or Active can be example property values; they are not the definition of a type.

practiceQuiz.scenario: A purchase succeeds in the application under test. How should the test keep an example OrderStatus property in TDS aligned with that verified result?

options.text: Assume every application action automatically updates TDS.
Explicitly update the known TDS item after verifying the application result.
Treat the TDS data view as proof that all application assertions passed.
Assume TDS plays no role in storing test data.

practiceQuiz.hint: Application state and test-data state are separate.
practiceQuiz.rationale: Use an explicit TDS update for the known item. Application actions and test execution reporting are not automatic synchronization of an ordinary stored property.

optionExplanations.A: TDS does not automatically mirror every application action into an ordinary stored property.
optionExplanations.B: The explicit update writes the required state to the known item after application verification.
optionExplanations.C: A stored value alone is not a report proving that all application assertions passed.
optionExplanations.D: TDS does store and manage test items; dismissing its role does not solve state management.

practiceQuiz.scenario: In this independent example, the purchase has succeeded and its next TDS Update step adds OrderNumber and sets OrderStatus to Pending. What does that configured step change?

options.text: The customer's Status changes from New to Active.
An OrderNumber column is created and OrderStatus is set to Pending.
The record is immediately moved to the 'Used' TDS type.
Nothing changes until the order is fully completed.

practiceQuiz.hint: Follow the explicitly stated update, not an assumed automatic lifecycle.
practiceQuiz.rationale: The configured update adds OrderNumber and sets OrderStatus to Pending. Other changes need separate configured operations; this example does not assert automatic DemoWebShop synchronization.

optionExplanations.A: The stated update does not change the customer Status property; that requires another operation.
optionExplanations.B: These are exactly the changes specified by the independent example Update step.
optionExplanations.C: Moving an item to Used requires a deliberate move operation; it is not part of this update.
optionExplanations.D: The configured Update changes the named properties now, not only after the entire order flow ends.

quickRecap.value: The configured data store that contains types.
A category of test items inside a repository.
One entry with its own properties.
Example Status properties need explicit updates; application changes are separate.
Find locks the selected item; ReadOnly does not acquire a lock.
Prepare necessary preconditions for focused tests rather than requiring every earlier test.
Move item to type explicitly moves a known item; Used is an example reuse policy.
